title: Temperature control reduced Liestal and Washington bloom correlation in 1988-2024, but not clearly in 1951-1987
abstract: We tested whether local February and March temperature control reduced annual cherry bloom correlation across Kyoto, Liestal and Washington. Six tests covered three site pairs in 1951-1987 and 1988-2024, with 37 common years per period. After site-specific linear time control, later Liestal and Washington had correlation 0.488. Added temperature control gave correlation -0.162. The reduction was 0.649, with a six-test adjusted block interval of 0.176 to 1.047. The other five reductions were uncertain. The later Liestal and Washington sign persisted with other block lengths, no trends, first differences and single-year deletions. Thus the temperature explanation did not give a clear result in both periods or across all pairs. Selected managed records, different bloom rules, missing visit logs, coarse weather and short periods limit inference. In-sample residual correlation does not establish a causal temperature effect. This study tests no air pollution or weather extreme. The package gives code, aggregate results, source hashes, rights notices and retrieval instructions. Restricted source dates and annual derivative records are excluded.

display.caption: Bloom correlations and reductions after February and March temperature control. Thick bars show 95 percent block intervals. Thin bars show six-test adjusted intervals. Only later Liestal and Washington had a clear primary reduction. Each period has 37 matched years.

citations.reason: Uses the same source archive and weather snapshot. Tests cross-site correlation rather than forecast errors. Biological records overlap; this is not independent validation.
